close_reason: Adopted option (a) from the bug report: documentation. Each of the four use-case-specific lints (Rfc5280EkuServerAuthLint, Rfc6125TlsServerSanLint, Rfc8398SmimeSanLint, Rfc8551EkuEmailProtectionLint) gained a '# Use-case applicability — operator contract' section in its struct-level rustdoc, naming its canonical LintProfile bundler and stating the operators-must-not-cross-bundle rule. Added a matching trait-level rustdoc section on Lint explaining the framework's stance: use-case selection is the LintProfile bundle's responsibility, the trait does not encode use case in its type signature. Considered option (c) self-narrowing via EKU but rejected after it broke check_basic_smime_shape's ability to gate (a TLS cert silently passing the S/MIME shape check is a worse failure mode than the original bug). Added two regression tests (use_case_mutual_exclusion_tls_cert_fails_smime_lints, use_case_mutual_exclusion_smime_cert_fails_tls_lints) that empirically verify the documented mutual-exclusion claim against real fixtures so the rustdoc cannot drift. All 126 lib tests pass; pkix-profiles tests pass; clippy --all-features clean. Sibling: PKIX-hy2e.4 (same fix).
description: Trigger: load any non-TLS-server end-entity certificate (S/MIME, code-signing, OCSP responder, time-stamping) and run rfc5280::Rfc5280EkuServerAuthLint against it. The lint declares applies_to() = SubjectKind::Leaf with no further qualification. RFC 5280 §4.2.1.12 only requires id-kp-serverAuth on TLS server certificates, not all leaves. Actual bad behavior: every non-TLS-server leaf produces LintResult::Error 'ExtendedKeyUsage does not include id-kp-serverAuth', poisoning EvaluationReport for any operator who registers the lint via a generic 'rfc5280-conformance' bundle. This trips the test corpus too: leaf-p256-365d-wrong-eku.der (used as a positive fixture in rfc8551 tests) is correctly rejected here only because the file happens to be intended for TLS-server-auth contexts. Same systemic shape as Rfc6125TlsServerSanLint, Rfc8398SmimeSanLint, Rfc8551EkuEmailProtectionLint — each lint silently assumes a use-case context but applies to any leaf. Fix options (any one): (a) document that these lints must only be registered by use-case-specific LintProfile implementations (currently no such warning); (b) gate via Lint::applies_to taking a use-case parameter; (c) have the lint inspect the cert's stated use-case from BasicConstraints + EKU + KeyUsage before firing. See lib.rs Lint trait documentation: there is no protection in the runner against registering mutually-exclusive use-case lints.
title: Rfc5280EkuServerAuthLint fires false positives on non-TLS-server leaves
